newsitem.title: USA: Stillwater Mining Q2 shr loss $0.03.
newsitem.headline: Stillwater Mining Q2 shr loss $0.03.

text.p: Stillwater Mining Company reported a net loss of $679,000, or three cents per share, on revenue of $22.3 million for the second quarter of 1997, compared to a net loss of $635,000, or three cents per share, on revenue of $10.7 million for the second quarter of 1996.

For the first six months of 1997, Stillwater reported a net loss of $2.9 million, or 14 cts per share, on revenue of $38.3 million compared to net income of $13.2 million, or 64 cts per share, on revenue of $24.3 million for the same period in 1996.
Before the effect of a change in accounting policy effective January 1, 1996, the company reported a loss of $645,000, or three cents per share, for the first six months of 1996.

With the completion of the approximately $70 million expansion at the Stillwater Mine, Nye, Montana, and the commissioning of the new 1,950 foot shaft, the operating performance at the mine has improved, chairman Ray Ballmer said in a statement.
For the second quarter of 1997, tons mined increased to 134,000, 40 pct higher than the same quarter in 1996.
Tons milled for the second quarter of 1997 were 134,000, a 24 pct increase over the same period in 1996.
This resulted in a 28 pct increase in production to 78,000 ounces of metal for the second quarter of 1997 compared to second quarter 1996 production of 61,000 ounces.

For the first six months of 1997 compared to the first six months of 1996, tons mined increased 37 pct to 255,000, and tons milled increased 26 pct to 255,000, resulting in a 34 pct increase in production to 157,000 ounces of platinum and palladium compared to 117,000 ounces for the first six months of 1996, Ballmer said.
"We are pleased that the expansion at the Stillwater Mine has been completed," Ballmer said.
"Now our goal is to attain the 2,000 ton-per-day milling rate and sustain it. In addition, we will be focusing on dilution control and improving our cost structure."
Revenue for the quarter was $22.3 million compared to $10.7 million for the second quarter of 1996.
The increase in revenue was due to an increase in ounces sold, 96,000 compared to 54,000 for the same period in 1996 and a higher average realized price for the quarter.

The increase in ounces sold in the second quarter was a result of higher production from the mine and processing of stockpiled mill concentrate that resulted from the rebricking of the smelter furnace in the first quarter of 1997.

For the first six months of 1997, revenue was $38.3 million as a result of higher ounces being sold, 178,000, compared to 117,000 ounces for the 1996 period, and a higher average realized price for the 1997 period compared to the 1996 period.
In addition, in the first quarter of 1997, Stillwater Mining changed its method of revenue recognition whereby revenue is now recognized when the metals are shipped from the base metals refinery.
The cost of metals sold for the second quarter of 1997 was $17.6 million compared to $9.9 million for the second quarter of 1996, as a result of higher production from the mine.
Cash costs per ounce were $189 for the second quarter of 1997 compared to $167 per ounce for the second quarter of 1996.
For the first six-months of 1997, cash costs per ounce were $186 compared to $175 per ounce for the same period in 1996.
The average realized price per ounce of platinum and palladium sold in the second quarter of 1997 was $232, $36 higher than the second quarter of 1996 figure of $196.
For the first six months of 1997, Stillwater Mining realized a price of $215 per ounce of metal sold compared to $208 for the same period in 1996.

The average combined price for the second quarter 1997, as quoted on the London Metals Exchange, was $227 per ounce. For the first six months of 1997, the average combined price was $208 as quoted on the London Metals Exchange.
